chunks: Certainly, what is in the hands of the people is right and wrong, true and false, repealing and repealed, general and particular, definite and indefinite, exact and surmised,

And false had been attributed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during his lifetime, so much so that he stood up to deliver a sermon and said: 'Whoever attributes falsehood to me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire.'

key_terms.مُحْكَمًا وَمُتَشَابِهًا: Definite and indefinite (clear and ambiguous verses)

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet warn against false attributions of his sayings?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi categorizes the sources of divergence in Hadith by listing binary opposites (such as nasikh/mansukh and muhkam/mutashabih) that characterize the textual corpus, reflecting the Shia emphasis on rigorous hadith criticism (ilm al-rijal). This passage underscores the historical reality of fabrication even during the Prophet's lifetime, necessitating a methodical approach to distinguish authentic traditions from those influenced by human error or deliberate deceit.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Certainly what is current among the people is both right and wrong, true and false, repealing and repealed, general and particular, definite and indefinite, exact and surmised.
Even during the Prophet’s days false sayings had been attributed to him, so much so that he had to say during his sermon that, “Whoever attributes falsehoods to me makes his abode in Hell.”
